the ways in which local agents, institutions and communities can create liveable cities in the face of the pressures of economic globalisation.
the ways in which local communities can be empowered to make places in cities that have become more global.
the social, economic and cultural dimensions of place making in the context of urbanisation and globalisation.

globalisation is a process that is not simply economic, but also cultural and political, and as such is not a single, linear process, but one that is complex, contradictory and uneven.
the globalisation of cities is a process that can be understood as both a threat and a promise to the liveability of the city.
